evals.prompt: I want to persist customer feedback in my Commerce app. Add a web runtime action that stores a feedback document in App Builder Database Storage and returns the result.
evals.expected_output: The agent installs @adobe/aio-lib-db, registers a web action (web: "yes") under a user package (not app-management) in src/commerce-extensibility-1/ext.config.yaml with include-ims-credentials: true, and creates a handler that resolves the injected IMS auth params with @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-auth, mints a raw access token string, calls init then connect, inserts into a collection, and closes the client in a finally block. It notes the workspace database must be provisioned (declaratively via the app.config.yaml database block on deploy, with the aio app db provision CLI as a local-dev fallback) and that the App Builder Data Services API must be added to the project in the Adobe Developer Console.
assertions: The action is registered with include-ims-credentials: true
The action package name is not 'app-management'
The handler calls init() then connect() and obtains a collection
The handler closes the client in a finally block

An IMS access token is obtained via getImsAuthProvider(resolveImsAuthParams(params)).getAccessToken() from @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-auth and passed to init() as a raw string (not generateAccessToken, not token.access_token)
The action is registered with web: "yes"
Provisioning (declarative auto-provision in app.config.yaml as primary, aio app db provision CLI as local-dev fallback) and the App Builder Data Services API are mentioned

evals.prompt: When an order is placed in Commerce, I want to record it in our database. The order event handler already needs to be created. Scaffold the event action and have it write the order to a collection.
evals.expected_output: The agent scaffolds an App Builder runtime action to consume the Commerce event (web: "no") registered with include-ims-credentials: true, reading the payload from params.data.value, and writing to a collection using the init/connect/close lifecycle. After build passes it suggests commerce-app-eventing to wire the action to the order event via runtimeActions.
assertions: The action is registered with include-ims-credentials: true
The handler reads the event payload from params.data.value
The handler uses init() -> connect() -> collection write -> close() in finally
The action is registered with web: "no"
Agent mentions commerce-app-eventing (or runtimeActions) to wire the action to the event

evals.prompt: Our workspace database is in emea. Add a runtime action that looks up a product by SKU from a 'products' collection, and make sure queries are efficient.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a handler that initializes the library with region 'emea' (matching provisioning), connects, queries the products collection by sku, and closes the client. It promotes best practices: creating an index on the queried field, using projections, and iterating cursors for large result sets.
assertions: init() is called with region: "emea"
The handler queries the products collection filtering by sku
The client is closed in a finally block
The agent recommends an index on the queried field and/or projections for efficiency
aio app build completes without errors

evals.prompt: When my Commerce app installs, create a 'held_orders' collection with a unique index on order_id so duplicate holds are rejected. Set it up as part of the app installation, not on first request.
evals.expected_output: The agent authors a custom installation step with defineCustomInstallationStep (install handler, ideally with an uninstall that drops the collection), exported as an ES module default export (export default, not module.exports), resolves the IMS auth params from context.params via @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-auth and mints a raw access token string, connects, gets the collection object and calls createIndex({ order_id: 1 }, { unique: true }) on it, and closes the client in a finally block. It wires the script into app.commerce.config.ts under installation.customInstallationSteps with a .js script path, a unique name, and a description.
assertions: The step is defined with defineCustomInstallationStep from @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-app/management
The IMS token is obtained via getImsAuthProvider(resolveImsAuthParams(context.params)).getAccessToken() from @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-auth (from context.params, not config; not generateAccessToken)
createIndex is called on a collection object with { order_id: 1 } and { unique: true }
The client is closed in a finally block
The step is registered under installation.customInstallationSteps in app.commerce.config.ts with a .js script path, a name, and a description
The install script is authored as an ES module using export default (not module.exports / CommonJS)

evals.prompt: My Commerce app is extension-only (no application runtime actions) and uses App Builder Database Storage. After aio app deploy the workspace database isn't provisioned. Configure it so the database is auto-provisioned on deploy.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that declarative auto-provision is skipped for extension-only apps because the application runtime manifest has no runtime action, and applies the workaround in app.config.yaml: an empty packages map (packages: {}) under application.runtimeManifest plus a post-app-build hook running mkdir -p dist/application/actions, alongside the database auto-provision block with a region. It may also mention the aio app db provision CLI as a local-dev fallback.
assertions: Identifies that auto-provision is skipped because the app has no application runtime action
Adds packages: {} under application.runtimeManifest
Adds a post-app-build hook running mkdir -p dist/application/actions
Keeps the database auto-provision block with a region
References the aio app db provision CLI as a local-dev fallback

evals.prompt: Add a web action that stores records in App Builder Database Storage. My repo has an app.commerce.config.ts at the root, but I haven't initialized the project yet — there's no src/commerce-extensibility-1/ directory and no node_modules.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes that although the config exists, the project is not initialized (no src/commerce-extensibility-1/ or node_modules), so it runs npx @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-app init before proceeding — without overwriting the existing config. Only after the project is initialized does it install @adobe/aio-lib-db and scaffold the storage web action.
assertions: The agent detects the project is not initialized despite the config being present
The agent runs npx @adobe/aio-commerce-lib-app init before doing storage work
The existing app.commerce.config.ts is not overwritten
Storage work (installing @adobe/aio-lib-db, scaffolding the action) proceeds only after initialization

evals.prompt: My initialized TypeScript Commerce app needs a storage web action and a custom installation step that creates a unique held_orders index. The app does not yet depend on @adobe/aio-lib-db. Use the skill's reference assets and validate the SDK-generated installation path with strict TypeScript checks and aio app build. Also run temporary compile-only probes confirming that numeric token and region inputs, an invalid index direction, and an unrelated type error are rejected. Remove all probes and rerun the final checks. Do not provision a database, deploy, or invoke the actions.
evals.expected_output: The agent installs @adobe/aio-lib-db without imposing a skill-specific version range and verifies the installed package supplies declarations. It uses both reference assets without ambient DB bridges or import suppressions. It registers scripts/setup-database.ts at the root installation.customInstallationSteps, regenerates the installation action, and verifies the generated import and actual compiler reachability without replacing existing includes. Strict typecheck and build pass without contacting a database. Compile-only probes reject numeric token/region inputs and invalid index directions through package-owned types, and an unrelated TypeScript error is still rejected. Probes are removed before final checks.
assertions: The library is installed without a skill-specific version range, and actual package declaration resolution is verified rather than inferred from the version
Package-owned declarations are used; no ambient DB bridges, import suppressions or disabled strict checking are introduced
Both the storage runtime asset and scripts/setup-database.ts are checked by the project's strict TypeScript configuration

Root installation.customInstallationSteps registration produces a generated import of scripts/setup-database.ts, which appears in the actual compiler file list without changing existing includes or exclusions
The project's strict typecheck and aio app build complete without errors
Compile-only numeric token/region and invalid index direction probes are rejected by package-owned types, and an unrelated TypeScript error is still rejected
Negative probes are removed and the final strict typecheck passes
No database provisioning, deployment or live database calls are performed

evals.prompt: Add TypeScript storage support to my initialized Commerce app. Inspect package.json, the lockfile, the installed @adobe/aio-lib-db package and src/types before changing files. This is an existing app: it may still be pinned to 1.0.4 with local DB declarations, or may already use 1.1.0. Do not change dependency pins or delete application declarations without approval.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the dependency, lockfile, installed package and actual declaration resolution, preserving existing ranges and pins. It uses package-owned types when available, otherwise compatible existing application declarations, and reports declaration conflicts without silently deleting application types. If neither source supplies types, it recommends an upgrade without requiring one or changing dependencies without approval; keeping the installed version uses documented ts-expect-error directives only on DB imports reporting TS7016. Strict typecheck and build run with both runtime and generated installation setup checked. The fallback is explicitly untyped; compilation is not runtime verification.
assertions: Declared, locked and installed versions and package declaration resolution are inspected; an existing app is not assumed to have upgraded
Existing dependency ranges and pins are preserved; an upgrade is recommended only when types are missing and is not required or performed without approval
Package-owned types are preferred, otherwise compatible existing application declarations are reused; no suppression is added when types resolve
Declaration conflicts are reported without silently deleting or overwriting application types
When neither package nor application types resolve, only DB imports reporting TS7016 receive documented ts-expect-error directives; no ambient bridges or broad suppressions are added
Unrelated declarations and existing strict compiler settings are preserved

Strict typecheck and build check both runtime and generated installation setup without changing includes; the fallback is acknowledged as untyped and compilation is not claimed as runtime verification

evals.prompt: My initialized TypeScript Commerce app pins @adobe/aio-lib-db to 1.0.4, with no package or application declarations. Keep that version and lockfile unchanged. Add a storage runtime action and custom installation step from the reference assets, then validate strict compilation and aio app build without provisioning, deploying or calling a database. Also run temporary compile-only probes confirming that removing the DB import suppressions reproduces TS7016 and an unrelated type error remains rejected. Restore the required directives, remove all probes and rerun the final checks.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies that no declarations resolve, mentions that package-owned types were introduced in 1.1.0 and recommends upgrading without forcing it. It keeps the pin and lockfile unchanged and adds documented ts-expect-error directives immediately above only the DB imports reporting TS7016. Root installation.customInstallationSteps registration produces the actual generated setup import, and both setup and runtime are checked. Strict typecheck and build pass; virtual removal of the directives reproduces TS7016 and an unrelated type error remains rejected. It acknowledges that DB calls remain untyped.
assertions: Actual missing declarations are verified and the existing dependency pin and lockfile are preserved
Only DB imports reporting TS7016 receive documented ts-expect-error directives; no ambient bridges or disabled strict checking are introduced
The generated installation imports setup and the actual compiler graph checks both setup and runtime without changing includes or exclusions
Strict typecheck and aio app build pass; removing directives reproduces TS7016 and an unrelated type error is rejected
Probes are removed before final checks; DB APIs are acknowledged as untyped and no database provisioning, deployment or live calls occur

evals.prompt: In my initialized Commerce app, add a web runtime action backed by App Builder Database Storage that queries active records. The public response should contain only title and status; records also contain a private internalMemo field. Explain inclusion and exclusion projections, including the _id exception. Do not provision or call a live database.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses an inclusion projection to select title and status, optionally excluding _id as the sole allowed exclusion. It explains that filters select documents while projections select fields, and inclusion and exclusion fields cannot be mixed except for _id. It does not claim that compiler or mocked checks prove live database acceptance.
assertions: Explains inclusion versus exclusion projections and that _id may be excluded alongside included fields
Distinguishes the query filter, which selects documents, from the projection, which selects returned fields
Uses explicit public-field inclusion without mixing private-field exclusions
Does not claim compiler or mocked checks prove live database acceptance or provision/call a live database
